name: Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd
title: Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd - 532732 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue Rs 279 cr (+19% YoY) and EBITDA Rs 52 cr (+29%, margin >19%) on 24% volume growth, but standalone slowing, no capacity signals, and cotton inflation flagged as a margin headwind.

triggers.label: Revised FY27 targets deferred to Q2
triggers.quote: we will let you know regarding the revised targets after the quarter 2 scenario.

triggers.label: Standalone growth slowing to ~12%
triggers.quote: 12% growth in this quarter, even last quarter was around 8%

guidance.quote: we will be growing from 15% to 18%. That was our revenue target.
we feel that the EBITDA margins will remain constant for the coming quarters.
The current target for our EBO would be around 50 to 70 odd stores for the current year on a net basis.
I think exports should remain flattish during the year.
The overall estimate for the other income should be at around Rs. 30 crores for the annualized year.

red_flags.quote: I would not like to comment on a standalone basis.

red_flags.label: Land monetisation stalled ~2 years
red_flags.quote: that is also in a standstill position

evasions.quote: I would not like to comment on a standalone basis. Let us look at a consolidated overview.

summary.headline: KKCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 279 crore, with EBITDA up 29% to Rs 52 crore at over 19% margin.
summary.overview:
Consolidated revenue reached Rs 279 crore, up 19% YoY, with apparel volumes up 24% and retail channel growth of 29%. EBITDA grew 29% YoY to Rs 52 crore and PAT grew 29% to Rs 41 crore, with EBITDA margin above 19% versus the 17-18% guided. Management said it crossed its 15-18% revenue target but declined to give standalone guidance or revise full-year targets until after Q2. Q&A focused on standalone growth, Lawman and Integrity revamps, Goregaon land and property monetisation, cotton cost inflation, and cash deployment for acquisitions.</overview>

segments.name: Killer
segments.commentary: Operates 464 exclusive brand outlets; same-store sales growth flat in the quarter.

segments.name: Kraus
segments.commentary: Strong sales growth with EBITDA margins in line with KKCL; management cites it as validating the acquisition integration. Focus on improving working capital cycle.

segments.name: Junior Killer
segments.commentary: Gaining traction across MBO and LFS as a kidswear entry; counter count rising.

segments.name: Lawman
segments.commentary: Shifting to a D2C-led model with 81 EBOs; management says the strategy change is now showing results, but the pivot is still being tested.

segments.name: Integrity
segments.commentary: Encouraging performance supported by renewed brand-building initiatives; no figures given.

segments.name: Jeans
segments.commentary: Contributes close to 50% of revenue; grew by double digits per management, though slower than the quarter's total growth.

guidance_outlook: Long-term aspiration to lift growth from 15% CAGR to 20% CAGR over three years via organic growth plus acquisitions (Vision 2028).
Revised full-year targets to be communicated after Q2 FY27; no quarter-to-quarter guidance given.
Net EBO addition target of around 50-70 stores for FY27; four net added in Q1, with openings concentrated in festive Q2 and Q3.
EBITDA margins expected to remain constant over coming quarters despite cotton cost increases.
Exports expected to remain flattish for the year.
Other income expected around Rs 30 crore for the full year.
No standalone growth guidance given; management directed analysts to consolidated view.
capex_capacity: Total EBO network at 670 as of June 30, 2026 after net addition of four in Q1 FY27.
EBO retail footprint above 4 lakh sq ft across 670 stores.
Goregaon property and land monetisation: in standstill; exploring development or outright sale, no timeline given.
Cash to be retained on balance sheet to fund a larger-ticket acquisition; acquisition pipeline under exploration but no deal timing given.
demand_pricing: Market described as challenging; management expects market share gains from brand repositioning.
Booking roadshow for summer season reported encouraging traction.
Cotton prices have risen; Q1 gross margin up by a percentage point (figure not specified), but management expects GP margin pressure ahead and is reducing discounts or passing cost to consumers.
Retail channel up 29% YoY; non-retail growth led by e-commerce, but non-retail grew below retail in Q1.
Exports primarily own-brand, skewed to Middle East.
Competition intensifying from large branded and conglomerate players; management cites hybrid manufacturing-wholesale-retail model rather than lower cost as edge.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone growth has lagged (12% this quarter, around 8% last); when will it pick up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the consolidated view (about 19%, above the 15-18% target) should be used; standalone Lawman and Integrity strategy changes have started to show results. Standalone guidance was declined later in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why are debtors rising over two years; what is the plan for Rs 400-500 crore cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors were flat QoQ and fell on a QoQ basis per management. Some cash will stay on the balance sheet to fund a bigger acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth guidance be raised given 19% in Q1 and festive-season skew?
qa_highlights.answer: No quarter-level guidance; revised targets will be given after Q2 results.

qa_highlights.question: Why is jeans share down to 9% from 12% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the figure: jeans are close to 50% of revenue and grew double digits; the 9% figure was another category, accessories/others, which is a low-GP trading item.

qa_highlights.question: Jeans growth slower this quarter; is there a shift to T-shirts and shirts?
qa_highlights.answer: Jeans grew double digits; strategy is to rationalise and focus on other categories, with basket size the value driver in retail.

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material inflation affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Cotton prices up; GP margin rose this quarter but may pressure GP ahead. Management is cutting discounts or passing on costs, and expects EBITDA margins to stay constant.

qa_highlights.question: Total sales realisation for the quarter including accessories?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stated 720 (figure as read on call); apparel realisation shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: Timing on Goregaon property monetisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is in talks but gave no deadline; will update once the deal is completed.

risks_watch: Cotton cost inflation may compress gross margin from Q2 onward; management hopes to offset through lower discounts and pricing.
Lawman and Integrity strategy changes are still being tested; standalone growth has lagged consolidated growth.
Killer same-store sales were flat in Q1.
Goregaon land and property monetisation has been pending for about two years with no firm timeline.
Acquisition pipeline and Kraus integration: deal timing unclear; cash on balance sheet is being held for a larger deal.
Management declined to comment on standalone growth or give timelines on pivots, limiting visibility.
Other income of around Rs 13 crore in Q1 is a sizeable share of PBT and needs monitoring.
summary.management_tone: Confident on consolidated numbers and brand strategy, but evasive on standalone performance, the Goregaon land, Lawman and Integrity pivots, and acquisition timing, repeatedly deferring details to later updates.
key_quotes: EBITDA margins remained strong at over 19%, exceeding a guidance of 17% to 18%, reflecting an efficient operational performance.
We definitely see that there has been an increase in cotton prices.
And we feel that the EBITDA margins will remain constant for the coming quarters.
Generally, we said that overall, on a consolidated basis, we will be growing from 15% to 18%.
